message.content: A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell** (sometimes referred to as a **syncytium**). Syncytia are formed when several cells fuse together, leaving a single cytoplasm with multiple nuclei. Examples include skeletal muscle fibers, osteoclasts, and certain giant cells seen in granulomatous inflammation.
